questions.question: According to section ________ of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934, the bank has full authority to issue banknotes of all denominations.

questions.question: How many states in India have a bicameral legislature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __6.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Bicameral structure means having both a Lower and Upper house, which mimics the structure of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha as- 

 
 
• Legislative Assembly/Vidhan Sabha. 
 
• Legislative Council/Vidhan Parishad.
 
 
 
• 
 
Currently, 6 states in India have a bicameral structure, which are

 
 
• 
 
Andhra Pradesh, 

 
 
• 
 
Uttar Pradesh, 

 
 
• 
 
Bihar, 

 
 
• 
 
Maharashtra,

 
 
• 
 
Karnataka and

 
 
• 
 
Telangana

 
 
 
 
• 
 
The remaining 22 states have a unicameral structure, which means they have only the Legislative Assembly and not the Legislative Council. 

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 
 
State legislature: 

 
 
• 
 
A state legislature is a legislative branch or body of a political subdivision in a federal system. For every state, there is a legislature, which consists of the Governor and one house or two houses.

 
 
 
 
• Articles 168 to 177: 
 
 
• "Deals with Constitution of Legislatures in States"- Article 168.
 
• "Abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in States"- Article 169.
 
• "Composition of the Legislative Assemblies"- Article 170.
 
• "To become a member of the state legislature"- Article 173.

questions.question: The government of India revised the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) in September 2021 by adding ________ drugs and deleting some.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __39.__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The government of India revised the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM) in September 2021 by adding** 39 drugs** and deleting some.
 
• The government has released 384 medicines under the National List of Essential Medicines (NLEM). 
 
• Health minister **Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya **released the updated version of NLEM 2022 at an event in New Delhi, on September 13.
 
• The NLEM 2022 contains 384 medicines as compared to 376 in NLEM, 2015. 
 
• The medicines have now been categorized into 27 therapeutic categories. A new section has been added for medicines considered essential for the supportive management of COVID-19.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The NLEM **is a dynamic document and is revised on a regular basis considering the changing public health priorities as well as advancements in pharmaceutical knowledge.
 
• The National List of Essential Medicines was first formulated in 1996 and it has been revised thrice in **2003, 2011, and 2015.**
 
• The NLEM, **revised every three years,** was last updated in 2015 and a revision was delayed due to Covid-19.
 
• The NLEM committee headed by **Balram Bhargava**, director general of the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), drafted a new NLEM.

questions.question: Inertia can be measured by its ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**mass.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Inertia can be measured by its mass.**
 
• **Mass is a measure of the inertia of the object, for an object, its inertia would depend on its mass.**
 
• **Inertia** is the property of an object by virtue of which it opposes any event that attempts to put the object in motion or to change its velocity.
 
• Therefore, an object at rest would want to continue staying at rest and an object in motion would have a tendency to continue its motion.
 
• The greater the mass of the object will be the tendency to resist the events.
 
• Hence, mass is a measure of the inertia of the object.
 
• **Newton's first law of motion:**
 
 
• It states that **"An object at rest stays at rest and an object in motion stays in motion with the same speed and in the same direction unless acted upon by an unbalanced force.**" Objects tend to "keep on doing what they're doing." In fact, it is the natural tendency of objects to resist changes in their state of motion. This tendency to resist changes in their **state of motion** is described as inertia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force:**

 
 
• The interaction that after applying to a body changes or try to change the state of motion or state of rest is called** force.**
 
• Force is denoted **by F and the SI unit is Newton (N).**
 
• **Force (F) = Mass (m) x acceleration (a).**

questions.question: Who was the viceroy of India when Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Northbrook.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Northbrook was the viceroy of India when Arya Samaj was founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati.**
 
• Lord Northbrook was appointed as viceroy of India from **1872 to 1876.**
 
• **"Arya Samaj":**
 
 
• This reform was one of the best movements for modern Hinduism.
 
• It was founded by **Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 AD**.
 
• Whose main purpose of **"Re-establishing the Vedas"**.
 
• Dayananda Saraswati gave the slogan** "Back to Vedas".**
 
• Dayananda Saraswati criticized evil practices like idolatry, caste system, untouchability, etc.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lord Curzon:**

 
 
• He was appointed as the Viceroy of India in the year 1899 and his Viceroyship ended in the year 1905.
 
• He became the Secretary of State for Foreign Affairs in 1919.
 
• MacDonnell Commission was appointed by Lord Curzon in 1901 and it submitted its report in the same year.
 
• Lord Curzon set up a Police Commission under Sir Andrew Frazer in 1902-03.
 
 
 
• **Lord Lansdowne (1888-1893):**
 
 
• During the term of Lord Lansdowne (1888-1893), Indian Council Act was passed in 1892.
 
• The significance of the Indian Council Act is to enlarge the Membership of central legislative councils.
 
• It transformed the viceroy's Executive Council into a miniature cabinet on the portfolio system.
 
 
 
• **Lord Dalhousie:**
 
 
• From 1848 to 1856, he was the Governor-General of India.
 
• His main intention was the expansion of British rule in India.
 
• The Doctrine of Lapse was introduced by him in India and he annexed eight states during his period.
 
• The Second Anglo Sikh was fought during his period and the whole of Punjab was brought under the British empire by him.

questions.question: Which ministry/institution has released the Provisional Estimates of National Income for the financial year 2019-20, both - at Constant Prices (2011-12) and Current Prices?
questions.solution:

• The Government of India through a resolution dated **1st June 2005 **set up the National Statistical Commission (NSC).
 
• The setting up of the NSC followed the decision of the Cabinet to accept the recommendations of the Rangarajan Commission, which reviewed the** Indian Statistical System in 2001**.
 
• The NSC was constituted with effect from 12th July 2006 with a mandate to evolve policies, priorities, and standards in statistical matters.
 
• The NSC has four Members besides a Chairperson, each having specialization and experience in specified statistical fields.
 
• The Commission has a part-time Chairperson, four part-time Members, and an ex- Officio Member.
 
• **The Chief Statistician of India,** the post created specifically as the Head of the National Statistical Office is the Secretary of the Commission.

questions.question: The _______ dam is built across the Subarnarekha river.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Chandil.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **In the Jharkhand state Chandil, the hydropower scheme is on the Subarnarekha river in the Seraikela Kharsawan district.**
 
• The project is a tripartite initiative among the three eastern states, Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odhisa.
 
• The main dam of the project is located at Chandil and another reservoir is located at Icha and two more barrages are located at Gauldih and Kharkiv.
 
• The main aim of the project is not only irrigation but also electricity generation for Jharkhand, West Bengal, and Odhisa.
 
• A loan of Rs 118 Crores for the construction of the project was sanctioned by the National Bank for Agricultural and Rural Development (NABARD).
 
• Initially, the World Bank from the USA (United States of America) sanctioned $127 Million but the funding was later withdrawn following the protest by the locals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
